pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #52737

Problem Summary:

We left a TODO to create a standalone `RangeFallbackHandler` rather than use a whole `*StatementContext`, because it's impossible to clone a whole `*StatementContext`.

### What changed and how does it work?

In this PR, I prepared a new smaller implementation of `*StatementContext`, and use it in the ranger context.

### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [ ] Integration test
- [ ] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
- [x] No need to test
  > - [ ] I checked and no code files have been changed.
  > <!-- Or your custom  "No need to test" reasons -->
  > The implementation is blindly copied from `StatementContext` implementation, and it's tested by existing tests about plan cache.

Side effects

- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU
- [ ] Performance regression: Consumes more Memory
- [ ] Breaking backward compatibility

Documentation

- [ ] Affects user behaviors
- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features
- [ ] Changes MySQL compatibility

issue_context.title: Don't use a whole `*StatementContext` as `RangeFallbackHandler`
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

We left a TODO for `RangeFallbackHandler`, because we are using a whole `*StatementContext` as the implementation of `RangeFallbackHandler`. We can extract some fields out of the statement context, and create a smaller implementation of `RangeFallbackHandler`.

review_comments: Is it better to rename it to `alwaysWarnSkipNoPreparedCache` because it only works on `SessionNonPrepared` ?

I think the semantic is to warn in any cases, but for other cases there is already a warn so it only applies to `SessionNonPrepared`.

It's used in `explain format='plan_cache'  xxx`. It should give a warning to show the status of any kinds of plan cache.
